result.topic_en: Riemann transforms the heat-conduction equation (I) to new curvilinear variables via a variational formulation, showing that the transformation reduces to transforming the quadratic differential form $\sum \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$.
result.transcription:
3

Iam in aequatione I loco coordinatarum rectangularium $x_1, x_2, x_3$
tres variabiles independentes novas $s_1, s_2, s_3$ introducamus. Haec
transformatio aequationis I facillime inde peti potest, quod haec
aequatio conditio est necessaria et sufficiens, ut designante $\delta u$ va-
riationem quamcunque infinite parvam ipsius $u$ integrale

(A) $\delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_{\iota'}} \partial x_1 \partial x_2 \partial x_3 + \iiint 2h \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} \delta u \, \partial x_1 \partial x_2 \partial x_3$

per corpus extensum tantum a valore variationis $\delta u$ in superfi-
cie pendeat. Introductis novis variabilibus haec expressio (A) transibit in

(B) $\delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial u}{\partial s_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial s_{\iota'}} \partial s_1 \partial s_2 \partial s_3 + \iiint 2k \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} \delta u \, \partial s_1 \partial s_2 \partial s_3$

posito brevitatis causa

[-$\sum a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial s_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} \frac{\partial s_\nu}{\partial x_{\iota'}}$ [?] $\frac{\partial s}{\partial x}$ [?]-] [-$\partial x$-]

$\sum a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial s_\mu}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial s_\nu}{\partial x_{\iota'}} \frac{1}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = b_{\mu,\nu}$ ; $\frac{h}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = k$.

Iam sint formarum secundi gradus

(1) $\begin{pmatrix} a_{1,1}, & a_{2,2}, & a_{3,3} \\ a_{2,3}, & a_{3,1}, & a_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$ (2) $\begin{pmatrix} b_{1,1}, & b_{2,2}, & b_{3,3} \\ b_{2,3}, & b_{3,1}, & b_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$

determinantes $A$, $B$, et formae adjunctae

(3) $\begin{pmatrix} \alpha_{1,1}, & \alpha_{2,2}, & \alpha_{3,3} \\ \alpha_{2,3}, & \alpha_{3,1}, & \alpha_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$ (4) $\begin{pmatrix} \beta_{1,1}, & \beta_{2,2}, & \beta_{3,3} \\ \beta_{2,3}, & \beta_{3,1}, & \beta_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$ ;

invenietur

$A = B \sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}$

et

$\beta_{\mu,\nu} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial x_\iota}{\partial s_\mu}\frac{\partial x_{\iota'}}{\partial s_\nu}$

ideoque

$\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ , $\frac{h}{A} = \frac{k}{B}$.

Unde facile perspicitur, transformationem aequationis (I) reduci posse
ad transformationem expressionis $\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$.

methods.what: Variational characterization of the heat equation: the equation holds iff the variation of the integral depends only on boundary values of the variation
methods.quote: $\delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_{\iota'}} \partial x_1 \partial x_2 \partial x_3 + \iiint 2h \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} \delta u \, \partial x_1 \partial x_2 \partial x_3$

methods.what: Transformation law of the conductivity coefficients under change of variables, including Jacobian factor
methods.quote: $\sum a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial s_\mu}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial s_\nu}{\partial x_{\iota'}} \frac{1}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = b_{\mu,\nu}$ ; $\frac{h}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = k$

methods.what: Relation between determinants of the original and transformed quadratic forms
methods.quote: $A = B \sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}$

methods.what: Adjoint (inverse) form transforms covariantly as a quadratic differential form (metric)
Invariance of the quadratic differential form and of the ratio h/determinant

items.english: This transformation of equation I can be obtained most easily from the fact that this equation is the necessary and sufficient condition that, with δu denoting any infinitely small variation of u, the integral (A) taken over the body depends only on the value of the variation δu on the surface.

items.quote:
Unde facile perspicitur, transformationem aequationis (I) reduci posse
ad transformationem expressionis $\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$.
items.english: Whence it is easily seen that the transformation of equation (I) can be reduced to the transformation of the expression Σ α dx dx.
